info.name: Taucho API
info.description:
Comprehensive Postman collection for the Taucho API.

Set {{baseUrl}} to switch environments (for example http://localhost:8081 or https://api.taucho.org).

Authentication notes:
- /auth/*, /oauth/*, and /niconico/* rely on the session cookie set by login or OAuth callbacks.
- Most resource endpoints (/watches, /conditions, /devices, /streams, /platform, /catalog, /custom-products, /live-events, etc.) expect an authenticated user context. When calling the API directly instead of through the portal proxy, include the X-User-ID header that your environment requires.

This collection includes all registered routes plus dedicated request variants for device template filtering.

request.description: Simple readiness probe for the Taucho API. Use this first to verify the service is reachable before testing authenticated or data-backed endpoints.
Returns API version and dependency availability. In the current implementation this endpoint is stubbed and returns 501 Not Implemented.
Reserved debugging endpoint. The route exists but currently returns a 501 placeholder response.
Creates a new local account immediately and sets the session cookie on success. Use this when email verification is not part of the desired flow.
Starts the email verification registration flow. The API stores a verification session, sends a one-time code by email, and returns the verification session ID needed by the next step.
Completes a verified signup by exchanging the verification session ID and emailed code for a real user account. The server sets the normal session cookie after success.
Authenticates using either email address or username plus password. A successful login refreshes the session cookie and returns the enriched user profile.
Clears the current portal session cookie. Use after login tests to verify logout and session invalidation behavior.
Returns the authenticated user profile including linked OAuth providers and NicoNico connection status. Requires the session cookie set by login or OAuth callback.
Updates mutable profile fields for the signed-in user. Both username and picture are optional, so you can patch either field independently.
Changes the local password for the authenticated user. This endpoint only works for accounts that already have a password set.
Permanently deletes the current user account and clears the session cookie. Useful for cleanup in end-to-end signup tests.
Lists all OAuth identities currently linked to the signed-in Taucho account. The response is useful before unlinking or troubleshooting discovery endpoints.
Removes one linked OAuth provider from the current account. The API protects against unlinking the final remaining login method.
Returns the provider-specific OAuth authorization URL as JSON and sets state cookies used by the callback flow. Supported providers depend on server configuration.
Completes Google OAuth sign-in or account linking. In a normal browser flow this endpoint sets the session cookie and redirects the user to the Taucho dashboard.
Completes Twitch OAuth and stores the Twitch token for platform discovery and follow lookups. Successful calls redirect to the dashboard after setting the session cookie.
Finishes Instagram OAuth login/linking. The callback stores tokens for later platform discovery and redirects to the dashboard on success.
Finalizes Facebook OAuth and links or creates the Taucho account. A successful callback redirects the browser to the dashboard.
Completes the Kick OAuth PKCE flow. The callback validates the stored verifier, stores the token, and redirects to the Taucho dashboard.
Completes TikTok OAuth and links the TikTok identity to the current or newly created Taucho account.
Completes X (Twitter) OAuth and stores the resulting token so the platform discovery endpoints can query the connected account later.
Reserved callback for Bilibili OAuth account linking. When configured, successful callback execution redirects to the dashboard like the other providers.
Meta/Facebook webhook for GDPR-style data deletion. Meta posts a form-encoded signed_request, Taucho deletes the linked account data, and responds with a confirmation URL/code payload.
Starts the authenticated NicoNico connection flow for an already signed-in Taucho user. Depending on the account, the response may either connect immediately or request an MFA follow-up call.
Completes the second-factor step for the authenticated NicoNico account-link flow and stores the resulting session cookie for future channel discovery.
Lets a user sign into Taucho directly with NicoNico credentials. If the NicoNico identity is new, Taucho creates or links the portal account automatically.
Completes the MFA step for the NicoNico-powered portal login flow and establishes the normal Taucho session on success.
Returns whether the current user has an active stored NicoNico session along with the linked Nico identity metadata when available.
Deletes the saved NicoNico session for the current Taucho user so future discovery and poller calls stop using that account.
Lists all watch targets for the current user. A watch target tells Taucho which creator/channel should be monitored for livestream starts.
Fetches one watch target by ID, including filters, status, and the most recent stream timestamps.
Creates a new watch target. If thumbnail_url is omitted, the server attempts to discover it automatically from the configured platform provider.
Partially updates a watch target. Use clear_filter or clear_thumbnail when you want to explicitly remove those optional values instead of replacing them.

request.description: Lists all conditions attached to a watch target. Each condition determines when Taucho should trigger a device action in response to live events.
Fetches one condition by ID after verifying that the current user owns the parent watch target.
Creates a rule that listens for a specific live event type and optionally evaluates additional logic before triggering a device action.
Partially updates an existing condition. You can change the event type, keyword filter, logic tree, target device, action, or action parameters.
Deletes the specified condition from the owning watch target.
Evaluates an unsaved logic tree against a synthetic live event payload. This is the fastest way to validate logic before creating or updating a real condition.
Loads an existing saved condition and evaluates it against a sample event. Set trigger_real_device to true only when you want the linked hardware API to be called.

request.description: Lists all devices for the current user using the safe summary representation. Sensitive credential fields are intentionally omitted from the list view.
Fetches one device record including stored credential metadata and group assignment details.
Registers a new user device. The device becomes configured immediately when credentials are provided in the create payload.
Updates editable device metadata and optionally replaces the stored credential payload for that specific device.
Deletes the selected device. Conditions referencing the device are cleaned up on the backend side.

Sends a real test command to the physical device through the template executor. The server validates that the template brand matches the device brand, resolves the user credential for that brand, and then calls the real device API.
Lists all device credentials for the current user. Sensitive fields are masked while still exposing enough metadata to identify which brand/device the credential belongs to.
Returns a single credential summary by numeric ID. The response still masks secrets such as API keys and bearer tokens.
Creates a new reusable brand credential. These credentials are later matched automatically by brand when devices or test commands are executed through the template system.
Updates one credential record. Only non-empty values are applied, which makes this endpoint convenient for rotating tokens or renaming the stored device.
Deletes the selected credential entry for the current user.
Lists available device templates. The current backend route exists, but without a brand or category filter it may return an empty array until a list-all implementation is added.
Returns all templates for a single supported brand. This is the main discovery call used before testing or building template-driven device commands.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Filters templates by category such as power, brightness, or color. Use this when building UX flows around a specific action type.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Returns the complete template definition, including endpoint URL, authentication strategy, body template, parameter defaults, UI fields, and example payloads.

response.name: 200 OK

request.description: Lists all device groups for the current user. Groups let Taucho coordinate multiple devices using sequential or queue semantics.
Fetches a single device group and includes the current list of device summaries assigned to that group.
Creates a new device group. Use option=sequential for rotating trigger order or option=queue for queue-style audience assignment.
Renames a device group and/or changes its coordination behavior.
Deletes the selected group container. Devices themselves remain, but their group association is removed.
Assigns a device to a group after verifying that both the device and the group belong to the current user.
Removes the current group assignment from a device without deleting the device itself.
Lists the user's own outbound stream accounts with stream keys masked in the response.
Returns a single outbound stream account record, including the full stream key for editing workflows.
Registers an outbound stream destination account that Taucho can track for your own live presence.
Partially updates an outbound stream account, including toggling whether it is active.
Deletes a saved outbound stream account entry.
Shows whether the background livestream poller is currently running. Useful for operational health checks and admin dashboards.
Starts the polling service if it is not already running.
Stops the polling service gracefully.
Returns the authenticated user's own YouTube channels using their stored Google OAuth token.
Returns a paginated list of channels the linked Google account is subscribed to.
Searches YouTube channels using the server-side API key. A linked Google account is not required for the search route itself.
Returns the linked Twitch account's own channel metadata using the stored user OAuth token.
Returns followed Twitch channels. The linked Twitch token must include the user:read:follows scope.
Searches Twitch channels. The backend can fall back to an app access token so this endpoint can still work without a user-linked Twitch account.
Returns the connected Instagram user account in a normalized Taucho response format.
Searches Instagram accounts using the provider client and returns normalized user results.
Returns Facebook Pages that belong to the linked Facebook account.
Searches Facebook Pages and returns a normalized Taucho page list.
Returns the authenticated user's linked TikTok account.
Searches TikTok creators and returns normalized user metadata.
Returns the linked X account in Taucho's normalized response shape.
Searches X users and returns a normalized result list.
Returns the linked Kick user's own channel using the stored Kick OAuth token.
Returns the Kick channels followed by the linked account, including the provider cursor when more pages are available.
Searches Kick using the unofficial public API and returns normalized channel results.
Returns the user or channel linked via the NicoNico semi-OAuth session stored on the Taucho side.
Searches public NicoNico live listings and returns deduplicated channel/community style results.
Reserved endpoint for returning the linked Bilibili space. The current implementation is a stub and responds with 501.
Reserved endpoint for listing Bilibili follows. It currently exists as a stub route and returns 501.
Searches Bilibili users through the public search API and returns normalized space records.
Lists catalog brands. By default only active brands are returned unless active_only=false is explicitly supplied.
Returns one brand together with all of its catalog products.

request.description: Creates a global brand record in the device catalog. This is primarily an admin-style endpoint rather than a normal end-user operation.
Updates a catalog brand in place. Only supplied fields are changed.
Deletes a catalog brand and, via database cascade, also removes its catalog products.
Lists catalog products, optionally filtered to a single brand.
Returns the full catalog record for one product model.
Creates a catalog product record for a specific brand and validates the supported_actions array against known Taucho device action names.
Updates product metadata and optionally replaces the supported action list.
Deletes a single product from the global catalog.
Lists all custom user-defined device products owned by the authenticated user.

Returns a single custom action and the custom product that owns it.

request.description: Creates a user-defined HTTP action for a custom product. The URL, headers, and body template can include placeholders resolved during execution.
Updates the metadata or HTTP request template for a custom action.
Deletes a custom action from the owning custom product.
Lists normalized real-time stream interactions such as comments, gifts, memberships, or superchats. Filter by stream_id, watch_id, and/or event_type as needed.
Returns one normalized live interaction event by ID, including sender, value, and raw provider payload metadata.
Returns a per-type aggregate count for a stream so dashboards can quickly summarize activity volume.
